questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A triangle has a base of 25 cm and a height of 6 cm. What is its area?

block.label: Quick Recall
block.sub: Four options, one answer — keep it fast

questions.why: Area equals ½ × base × height, so ½ × 25 × 6 = 75 cm². Rushing to skip the halving step gives double the real answer.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A cuboid is 5 cm long, 4 cm wide, and 3 cm high. What is its total surface area?

block.label: Scrub It
block.sub: Rub out the wrong answers with your finger

questions.why: Add the areas of all six faces: 2(5×4) + 2(5×3) + 2(4×3) = 40+30+24 = 94 cm². A common error is only finding the volume (60 cm³) or forgetting to double each pair of faces.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: What do we call a container that lets no gas or matter escape during a reaction?
questions.why: A closed (sealed) system traps all gases and matter, so no mass can escape or enter — this is why mass appears conserved.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: What is it called when a chemical reaction produces a colour change?

questions.subject: PDHPE
questions.prompt: What marketing trick makes a snack seem healthier than it actually is?
questions.why: Words like 'natural' or 'low fat' on packaging can make a snack appear healthier than its full nutrition label shows.

questions.subject: PDHPE
questions.prompt: On a nutrition label, what does the energy value usually measure in?
questions.why: Energy on an Australian nutrition label is given in kilojoules (kJ), not grams or milligrams, which are used for nutrients like fat or sugar.
